## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6) is the sixth treatise of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Ronkin 2005]. It provides a systematic analytical treatment of the twelvefold formula of dependent origination (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) [Ronkin 2005]. The canonical exposition is later interpreted and expanded in the commentary *Sammohavinodanī*, which investigates the twelve links (*nidāna*) in light of the twenty-four conditional relations (*paccaya*), examining how each factor—such as ignorance (*avijjā*) in relation to volitional formations (*saṅkhāra*)—operates across conscious moments as an object condition, a decisive support condition, a root cause, or through conascence and mutuality [Ronkin 2005].

 DharmaNexus indicates massive internal text reuse across the Pali Canon, most prominently sharing over 3,000 matching segments with the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), as well as extensive parallels with the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (e.g. Ds 2.1.1, Ds 2.1.6–8, Ds 2.3.3), the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, the *Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta* (MN 38), other chapters of the *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 12, Vb 15), and the *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the treatise across languages with Sanskrit texts on dependent origination, notably the *Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśasūtra*, the *Nidānasaṃyukta*, and the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* (along with Vīryaśrīdatta's *Nibandhana*), as well as corresponding Tibetan translations (D 317, D 3996) and Chinese Āgama texts (*Saṃyuktāgama*, T 99, T 124; *Ekottarikāgama*, T 125) [DharmaNexus].
